theCrux.twoDifferentInstrumentsForTheSameWord: 'Bastrop's residue' has meant two different, non-comparable things across this program's lanes. CTX-STAGE2's counting rule (which a prior, defective CTX-SP dispatch wrongly specified) is ST_Contains(polygon, ST_PointOnSurface(parcel)) against landing_parcel_jurisdiction -- a raw point-in-polygon test with its own denominator. The RAIL this file actually gates (parcel-r5-zoning's own processCity / CHUNK_ZONE_MATCH_SQL) uses best-overlap ST_Covers with an ST_Intersects + 1e-8 ring-area floor fallback and a bbox-centre fallback for parcels lacking usable ring geometry, ranked by overlap area, sourced from CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL's own in-city population. CTX-SP's own close already flagged its 48-before/48-after as an unexplained free finding under the WRONG instrument; this dispatch's fix is to measure with the RIGHT one and not import any number, including CTX-STAMPFALL's own expected 26, without independently reproducing it.
theCrux.howTheMeasurementDoublesAsTheInstrument: assertResidueWithinDeclaration fires INSIDE processCity, unconditional on the apply flag -- so calling runParcelR5Zoning directly with the CURRENT (unedited) declaration, where Bastrop's ceiling is still 9, is expected to throw LAYER_GAP_RESIDUE_EXCEEDED, and the thrown error's own actualResidue field IS the rail's live, real measurement. This is not a workaround; it is the intended mechanism the dispatch is pointing at by insisting on a direct call rather than cli.mjs.
